To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the degree of unbunding in electricity markets is negatively affected by the budgetary interests of regulatory authorities and that this effect is stronger, the more electricity is subject to a specific tax.
the degree of liberalization of an electricity market is negatively related to the budgetary interests of its regulators.
the more budgetary interests are present in the regulatory process, the more likely is the electricity sector not to be fully liberalized.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to avoid regulatory capture in electricity markets and how to achieve a more efficient unbundling of the industry.
the question how to design regulatory agencies that are able to pursue competition policy in the electricity sector despite their financial dependency on governments.
the question whether the budgetary interests of regulatory authorities are a significant determinant of the liberalization of electricity markets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the less the budgetary interests of regulatory decision makers are affected by the degree of unbunding of the electricity industry, the higher the degree of unbungling in the electricity industry.
the degree of unbunding is negatively correlated with the budgetary interests of regulators.
the more a regulator is dependent on the government's budget for its own financing, the less it is likely to implement unbundling measures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
budgetary interests of regulators are a major obstacle to unbundling in OECD electricity markets.
a clear separation of regulatory and budgetary interests is an important precondition for the success of liberalization.
the more a regulator's budget depends on the revenues from the regulated industry, the less liberalized this industry will be.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the degree to which electricity markets are unbundled from other industries is a crucial indicator for the level of competition.
the more the budget of a regulatory agency depends on revenues from the regulated industry, the less liberalization in this sector is to be expected.
the more clearly budgetary interests and regulatory goals are separated, the higher is the likelihood that a step towards liberalization will be implemented.
